rows.title: RESTler: Stateful REST API Fuzzing
rows.venue: IEEE/ACM International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE)
rows.authors: Vaggelis Atlidakis; Patrice Godefroid; Marina Polishchuk
rows.abstract: This paper introduces RESTler, the first stateful REST API fuzzer. rows.title: WuppieFuzz: Coverage-Guided, Stateful REST API Fuzzing
rows.venue: International Conference on Information Systems Security and Privacy (ICISSP)
rows.authors: Thomas Rooijakkers; Anne Nijsten; Cristian Daniele; Erieke Weitenberg
rows.abstract: Many business processes currently depend on web services, often using REST APIs for communication. REST APIs expose web service functionality through endpoints, allowing easy client interaction over the Internet. To reduce the security risk resulting from exposed endpoints, thorough testing is desired. Due to the generally vast number of endpoints, automated testing techniques, like fuzzing, are of interest. rows.title: Fuzzers for Stateful Systems: Survey and Research Directions
rows.authors: Cristian Daniele; Seyed Behnam Andarzian; Erik Poll
rows.abstract: Fuzzing is a very effective testing methodology to find bugs. In a nutshell, a fuzzer sends many slightly malformed messages to the software under test, hoping for crashes or incorrect system behaviour. The methodology is relatively simple, although applications that keep internal states are challenging to fuzz. The research community has responded to this challenge by developing fuzzers tailored to stateful systems, but a clear understanding of the variety of strategies is still missing. rows.title: Differential regression testing for REST APIs
rows.venue: ACM SIGSOFT International Symposium on Software Testing and Analysis (ISSTA)
rows.authors: Patrice Godefroid; Daniel Lehmann; Marina Polishchuk
rows.abstract: Cloud services are programmatically accessed through REST APIs. Since REST APIs are constantly evolving, an important problem is how to prevent breaking changes of APIs, while supporting several different versions. To find such breaking changes in an automated way, we introduce differential regression testing for REST APIs. Our approach is based on two observations.
